question: Who was the chief coordinator for the G20 summit hosted by India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Harsh Vardhan Shringla**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• Harsh Vardhan Shringla is a retired Indian diplomat who served as the Foreign Secretary of India.

• He was appointed as the Chief Coordinator for the G20 summit hosted by India in 2023.

• His role involved coordinating the various activities and logistics associated with hosting the summit.

• His extensive experience in diplomacy and international relations made him a suitable choice for this critical role.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **G20 Summit**

• The G20 is an international forum for governments and central bank governors from 19 countries and the European Union.

• Founded in 1999, it aims to discuss policy pertaining to the promotion of international financial stability.

• The G20 includes the world's major economies and accounts for about 85% of global GDP and 75% of international trade.

• The summit is held annually, and each member country takes turns to host the meeting.

• **Role of a Chief Coordinator**

• The Chief Coordinator is responsible for overseeing the planning, organization, and execution of the summit.

• This role involves coordinating with various government departments, international organizations, and other stakeholders.

• The Chief Coordinator ensures that all logistical and administrative arrangements are in place for the smooth conduct of the summit.

• The role is crucial for the successful hosting of such a large and significant international event.

• **Harsh Vardhan Shringla's Career**

• Harsh Vardhan Shringla joined the Indian Foreign Service in 1984.

• He has served in various capacities in Indian missions in Paris, Washington D.C., and Bangkok.

• He has also served as the Ambassador of India to the United States, Thailand, and Bangladesh.

• He was appointed as the Foreign Secretary of India in January 2020 and served until April 2022.
